AI-ConneX

DATA STUDIO — IF/ELSE CONDITIONING & INDUSTRIAL VISUALIZATION DEPLOYMENT GATE

Post–Feature Engineer Decision Node | Compliance Report #6

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

The AI-ConneX IF/ELSE Conditioning Node is the controlled decision gate immediately after Feature Engineer (FE). Its job is not to perform another generic transformation. It determines what the user actually wants to do with the engineered data: deploy it as an industrial Data Studio Microservice/Service for organization, mathematical/physics-aware analysis and visualization, or route the workflow to ML Studio when the intent is explicitly model-oriented.

CHATBOT INTENT      |      vBRAIN Compiler -> Profiler -> DAG -> Recipe Orchestrator      |      vPREPARE      |      vFEATURE ENGINEER      |      v+--------------------------------+| IF / ELSE CONDITIONING NODE    ||                                || IF intent = DATA/SERVICE       ||       -> DEPLOYMENT NODE       ||       -> Physics/Math Layer    ||       -> Visualization Service ||                                || ELSE IF intent = MODEL/ML      ||       -> ML STUDIO             ||                                || ELSE                           ||       -> clarification/gate    |+--------------------------------+

The architectural principle is: **do not force an ML model where a deterministic mathematical/physics visualization service already solves the industrial problem.** Many industrial users need better organization, monitoring, signal interpretation, derived measurements, engineering views, anomaly marking, and interactive visualization rather than prediction.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 2. Why This Decision Node Exists | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

Feature engineering can produce a useful analytical representation even when no machine-learning model is required. An industrialist may want to visualize vibration spectra, compare machine cycles, inspect pressure/flow relationships, monitor energy consumption, detect threshold violations, calculate FFT/PSD, overlay engineering limits, or explore process behavior. These tasks can be delivered as deterministic services.

Conversely, if the user's intent is predictive, classificatory, forecasting, recommendation-oriented or explicitly model-driven, the engineered feature package should go to ML Studio rather than being silently converted into a visualization service.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 3. The Core IF/ELSE Rule | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

IF user_intent.requires_model == TRUE:       route = ML_STUDIOELSE IF user_intent.requires_service == TRUE     OR user_intent.requires_visualization == TRUE     OR user_intent.requires_analysis == TRUE:       route = DEPLOYMENT_NODEELSE:       route = CLARIFICATION_GATE

The actual implementation should use a structured intent contract from the Brain rather than parsing raw chatbot text at this late stage.

section: 4. Why the Gate Is AFTER Feature Engineer
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 4. Why the Gate Is AFTER Feature Engineer | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

The gate is intentionally placed after FE because the decision has to be made against the final analytical representation that will actually be consumed. By this point, AI-ConneX has already established dataset identity, data quality, entity/time semantics, DAG constraints, preparation logic, feature definitions and lineage.

| Earlier location | Why it is insufficient |
| --- | --- |
| After Chatbot | Intent is known, but dataset suitability and engineered representation are not |
| After Compiler | Format is unified, but analytical semantics are incomplete |
| After Profiler | Profile describes data, but useful derived features may not yet exist |
| After DAG | Workflow is known, but feature output is not final |
| After Recipe Orchestrator | Preparation/FE plans exist, but final feature availability is not guaranteed |
| After PREPARE | Clean data exists, but FE may create required analytical signals |
| After FE | Final feature package + intent + lineage are available; routing is informed and deterministic |

[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

Deployment here does not necessarily mean deploying an ML model. It means exposing a reusable industrial data service. The service can accept data, calculate deterministic mathematical/physics-derived quantities, organize them into views, and return interactive or machine-readable outputs.

Industrial Dataset      |      vData Service  |  +--> normalized views  +--> mathematical transforms  +--> physics-derived quantities  +--> annotations  +--> visualization API  +--> export API  |  vBrowser / HMI / SCADA-adjacent dashboard / Engineering workstation

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 10. The Mathematical & Physics Layer | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

When a service deployment is selected, an Agent Helper can construct a controlled Mathematical & Physics Layer. The agent chooses from approved mathematical and domain primitives based on dataset type, profile and intent.

FFT / inverse FFT

Power spectral density

RMS / peak / crest factor

Moving statistics

Derivative / integral

Rate of change

Correlation / cross-correlation

Frequency-band energy

Pressure-flow relationships

Energy/power calculations where units are known

Mass/volume flow relationships where validated

Engineering threshold overlays

Cycle alignment

Operating-state segmentation

The agent should not invent a physical law. Every physics formula must carry units, assumptions, parameter provenance and a domain validation status.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 11. Agent Responsibilities | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]



| Agent may | Agent must not |
| --- | --- |
| Select approved math primitive | Invent an unvalidated physical law |
| Infer likely visualization type | Silently alter source data |
| Suggest thresholds from configured domain metadata | Present guessed thresholds as certified limits |
| Generate visualization configuration | Bypass security controls |
| Compose deterministic transformations | Execute unrestricted arbitrary code |
| Explain derived quantities | Claim engineering certification without evidence |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 13. FFT Use Case | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

For vibration, acoustic, electrical and rotating-equipment datasets, an FFT-based service can transform a time-domain signal into a frequency-domain representation. The service can mark frequency peaks, harmonics, configured bands and engineering reference regions.

TIME DOMAINsensor(t) |  |  |  |  | v  v  v  v  vFFT | vFREQUENCY DOMAINHz --> amplitude |       | |       +--> peak marker +----------> band marker

FFT requires explicit sampling assumptions. The service must know or validate the sampling frequency and windowing configuration; otherwise the frequency axis can be wrong.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 14. Example FFT Visualization | Authority: A]

The system should label these as observations or configured interpretations, not automatically diagnose a mechanical fault unless an approved diagnostic rule/model exists.

section: 17. Industrial Use Case 1 — Predictive Maintenance WITHOUT ML
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 17. Industrial Use Case 1 — Predictive Maintenance WITHOUT ML | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

A plant may not want a model. It may simply want a service showing vibration FFTs for each machine and automatically marking dominant frequency bands. Engineers can inspect whether the spectrum has changed from a baseline.

This provides immediate engineering value without model training, labels or an ML lifecycle.

section: 33. Why the IF/ELSE Node Must Not Be an Agent-Only Decision
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 33. Why the IF/ELSE Node Must Not Be an Agent-Only Decision | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

An agent can interpret intent, but a deterministic policy engine should make the final route. This is important because the route has operational consequences: ML Studio may create a training lifecycle, while Deployment may expose a service. The system should not allow probabilistic language interpretation alone to choose a production path.

Agent interpretation        |        vStructured intent        |        vDeterministic policy engine        |    +---+---+    |       |  ML      SERVICE

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 34. Decision Confidence | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

Where natural-language intent is ambiguous, the system should not guess. For example, 'show me whether the pump will fail' could mean a visualization of historical failures or a predictive model. The gate should request clarification or use an explicit Brain-level intent contract.

| Intent state | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Explicit model=true | ML Studio |
| Explicit service=true | Deployment |
| Visualization=true, model=false | Deployment |
| Analysis=true, model=false | Deployment |
| Ambiguous | Clarification |
| Policy violation | Block |

section: 35. Why Not Deploy Directly After PREPARE?
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 35. Why Not Deploy Directly After PREPARE? | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

Because FE may create the exact derived signals required for useful visualization or downstream model input. If deployment happens before FE, later feature definitions can diverge between analytical and deployed paths. FE provides the stable analytical contract that both branches can consume.

section: 36. Why Not Put the Gate After ML Studio?
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 36. Why Not Put the Gate After ML Studio? | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

That would be architecturally wrong because ML Studio is itself a downstream specialization. The purpose of the gate is to choose whether ML Studio is needed. Sending every workload into ML first introduces unnecessary training, evaluation, model governance and maintenance overhead.

section: 37. Why Not Put the Gate in the Brain?
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 37. Why Not Put the Gate in the Brain? | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

The Brain should understand and plan the workflow, and it may propose the route. However, the final routing gate belongs after FE because the system now has the final feature package and can verify that the requested service/model path is technically possible. This creates a defense-in-depth architecture: Brain plans; the post-FE gate validates and commits the route.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 38. Routing Algorithm | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

def route(ctx):    if not ctx.fe_report.pass_status:        return BLOCK    if ctx.intent.requires_model:        return ML_STUDIO    if (        ctx.intent.requires_service        or ctx.intent.requires_visualization        or ctx.intent.requires_analysis    ):        return DEPLOYMENT    return CLARIFICATION

Production implementation should also include policy, security, resource and compatibility checks.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 40. Mathematical Layer Validation | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

The mathematical layer must validate numerical assumptions. For FFT, for example, the sampling rate determines the frequency axis. If the sampling frequency is missing or inconsistent, the system should block or explicitly mark the result as invalid rather than producing a visually convincing but incorrect spectrum.

Sampling-rate validation.

Uniform/irregular timestamp detection.

Window-size validation.

FFT-size validation.

NaN/Inf handling.

section: 54. Failure: Visualization That Looks Correct but Is Wrong
text:
[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 54. Failure: Visualization That Looks Correct but Is Wrong | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

A major industrial risk is a visually attractive chart built from incorrect sampling, units, timestamps or aggregation. AI-ConneX therefore treats visualization as an analytical result requiring contracts and validation, not as a cosmetic frontend operation.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 55. Failure: Physics Formula Without Units | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

For example, adding pressure in bar to pressure in psi is numerically possible but physically meaningless. The Physics Layer must require compatible units before calculation. Where unit conversion is needed, the conversion should be explicit and lineage-tracked.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 56. Failure: Too Much Visualization | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

An agent can generate dozens of charts that overwhelm operators. AI-ConneX should optimize for task relevance: the user's intent plus profiler metadata determine the minimum useful set of visualizations.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 57. Failure: Service vs Model Confusion | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

A deterministic threshold visualization should not be marketed as AI prediction. Conversely, if the user explicitly asks for a failure probability, the system must route to ML Studio. Clear separation improves governance, explainability and lifecycle management.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 64. Industrial Value Proposition | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

AI-ConneX becomes more useful to industry when it does not equate 'AI' with 'ML model'. A plant may have years of sensor data but no reliable failure labels. It may still obtain immediate value from data unification, deterministic calculations, frequency analysis, engineering visualization, threshold monitoring and structured reporting.

No model training cost.

No model retraining lifecycle.

Deterministic results.

High explainability.

Works with small datasets.

Useful with legacy equipment.

Can run on CPU infrastructure.

Can expose APIs to existing systems.

Can support engineers rather than replace them.

Can later become an ML input when enough evidence exists.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-007-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Data Studio IF ELSE CONDITIONING Documentation | Studio: DataStudio | Category: StateTransition | Section: 67. Final Design Principle | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: ConditionalRouter, RuleEngine, BranchEvaluator]

The IF/ELSE Conditioning Node is the architectural point where AI-ConneX decides whether the engineered data should become a model input or an industrial analytical service. It prevents the system from over-engineering simple problems with ML while ensuring genuine model requests are not weakened into visualization-only services.

The governing rule is: **If the industrial problem can be solved deterministically and the user wants organization, analysis or visualization, deploy a governed Data Studio service. If the user needs prediction, classification, forecasting, optimization or another learned model, route to ML Studio. If the intent is ambiguous, ask rather than guess.**
